name: Engine 2 Diet

card.summary: The Engine 2 Diet is a whole-food, plant-based eating plan by Rip Esselstyn that people use to lower weight and body fat for a leaner look.

quick.overview:
The Engine 2 Diet is a low-fat, whole-food, plant-based plan created by former firefighter and triathlete Rip Esselstyn. It excludes animal products and processed foods and was popularised by a 2009 book with a 28-day program.

The appearance link is weight and body-fat loss: the book's subtitle promises lower cholesterol and shed pounds. Leaner body composition is the looks payoff followers cite.
quick.how: Followers eat whole grains, legumes, vegetables and fruit and avoid meat, dairy, eggs and processed foods, often starting with the 28-day program in the book.
quick.risks: Fully plant-based diets generally call for attention to nutrients such as vitamin B12; people with medical conditions are usually advised to consult a clinician.

lead: The Engine 2 Diet is a low-fat, whole-food, plant-based diet created by Rip Esselstyn, a former Austin, Texas firefighter and triathlete. It excludes all animal products and processed foods.[1]

It began in 2003 when a colleague at Esselstyn's Engine 2 firehouse learned he had very high cholesterol and Esselstyn encouraged the crew to switch to plant-based eating. The resulting book, The Engine 2 Diet (2009), carries a foreword by T. Colin Campbell and reached the New York Times best-seller list. In 2019 the brand was renamed PLANTSTRONG.[1]
People use it to lose weight and become leaner; the book's subtitle claims it lowers cholesterol and burns away pounds over a 28-day plan.[1]

chain: Eat whole plant foods, no animal products or processed foods
Lower calorie density and fat intake
Weight and body-fat loss, leaner look
angle.text: Followers adopt the plan to drop weight, which they associate with a leaner face and body. The mechanism is overall energy intake.

paras: The plan is described as plant-based, low-fat and whole-food, and Esselstyn calls the approach "plant strong".[1] Follow-up books include My Beef With Meat (2013) and The Engine 2 Seven-Day Rescue Diet.[1]
No studies found specifically testing the Engine 2 Diet are cited in general references.[1]

timeline.event: Firehouse colleague's cholesterol result prompts the diet switch.[1]
